Are you a resident of Prince George's County and have some legal issues to take care of? Or maybe you're just curious about the county's legal system? Either way, this article is for you. In this article, we will discuss everything you need to know about Prince George's County Circuit Court, from its history and jurisdiction to its procedures and services.

History of Prince George's County Circuit Court

The Prince George's County Circuit Court was established in 1798, shortly after the formation of Prince George's County. It was one of the first circuit courts in Maryland and has been in continuous operation since its establishment. The court has undergone several renovations and expansions over the years to accommodate the county's growing population and caseload.

Jurisdiction of Prince George's County Circuit Court

The Prince George's County Circuit Court is a trial court of general jurisdiction, which means that it has the authority to hear a wide range of cases. Its jurisdiction includes civil, criminal, family, and juvenile cases. It also has concurrent jurisdiction with the district court in some types of cases.

Structure of Prince George's County Circuit Court

Judges

The Prince George's County Circuit Court is presided over by 13 judges who are appointed by the governor with the advice and consent of the Senate. They serve a term of 15 years and may be reappointed for an additional term. The judges are responsible for presiding over trials, hearings, and other legal proceedings in the court.

Clerks

The clerks of the Prince George's County Circuit Court are responsible for maintaining the court's records and providing administrative support to the judges. They are appointed by the judges and serve at their pleasure.

Courtrooms

The Prince George's County Circuit Court has multiple courtrooms located in the courthouse in Upper Marlboro. The courtrooms are equipped with modern technology to facilitate the conduct of legal proceedings.

Procedures in Prince George's County Circuit Court

Filing a case

To file a case in the Prince George's County Circuit Court, you must first determine which division of the court has jurisdiction over your case. You can then obtain the necessary forms from the court's website or the clerk's office and file them with the appropriate division.

Serving notice

After filing a case, you must serve notice of the lawsuit on the other party. This is usually done by a sheriff or other authorized process server.

Pretrial conferences

Before a trial, the court may hold a pretrial conference to discuss the case with the parties and attempt to resolve any issues or disputes.

Trials

Trials in the Prince George's County Circuit Court are generally conducted before a judge and a jury. The parties present their evidence and arguments, and the jury makes a decision based on the facts of the case.

Appeals

If a party is dissatisfied with the decision of the Prince George's County Circuit Court, they may file an appeal with the Maryland Court of Special Appeals. The Court of Special Appeals will review the case and determine whether the circuit court made any errors in its decision.

Services provided by Prince George's County Circuit Court

Family Division

The Family Division of the Prince George's County Circuit Court handles cases related to domestic relations, such as divorce, child custody, child support, and domestic violence. The court offers mediation services to help parties reach an agreement on these issues.

Juvenile Division

The Juvenile Division of the Prince George's County Circuit Court handles cases involving minors who are accused of committing a crime. The court also offers programs to help juvenile offenders rehabilitate and reintegrate into society.

Criminal Division

The Criminal Division of the Prince George's County Circuit Court handles cases involving felony offenses, such as murder, robbery, and drug offenses. The court also oversees the county's drug court program, which provides treatment and supervision to nonviolent drug offenders.

Civil Division

The Civil Division of the Prince George's County Circuit Court handles cases involving disputes between individuals or entities, such as breach of contract, personal injury, and property disputes. The court also offers alternative dispute resolution services, such as mediation and arbitration, to help parties resolve their disputes outside of court.

The Civil Clerk of the Prince George's County Circuit Court is responsible for managing and maintaining records and proceedings related to civil cases, such as personal injury claims, breach of contract disputes, and property disputes.

Criminal Clerk

The Criminal Clerk of the Prince George's County Circuit Court is responsible for managing and maintaining records and proceedings related to criminal cases, such as felony offenses, misdemeanors, and traffic violations.
